extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers preparing submissions for the BBC National Short Story Award (British nationals / UK residents)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a short story (up to 8,000 words) for consideration in the BBC National Short Story Award, judged on originality, emotional resonance, and technical craft with attention to innovation vs accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: A genuine claim to newness — fresh subject, fresh approach, or fresh language. Distinguishes the prize-winner from competent execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality should be substantive (voice, subject, or technique) and not novelty for its own sake; the story must offer something that sets it apart from otherwise well-executed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional Resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: The story must move the reader. Affective power is decisive in the compressed form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges value emotional impact and humane perspective; Judge Di Speirs cited 'compassion and understanding' as the binding quality of selected stories. Evaluate whether the story elicits sustained feeling or insight rather than mere cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastery of the short form's particular demands — economy, suggestion, structural unity, last-line landing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess economy of language, effective use of suggestion rather than over-explication, coherent structure that supports a compressed arc, and a resonant closing line. Look for precision, control of pacing, and technical choices that serve the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of Innovation and Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges explicitly balance innovation (formal risk, originality of voice) against accessibility (the story must reach a serious reading audience, not only specialist readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A story that is innovative but unreadable does not win; a story that is accessible but conventional does not win. Evaluate whether formal or linguistic risk enhances rather than blocks reader engagement and whether voice/originality communicates to a serious reading public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with Moral/Cultural Weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Affinity for stories that engage serious moral or cultural matters — e.g., collision of cultures leading to new comprehension; the need to adapt in hardship; compassion across difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These recurring thematic notes indicate judges' preferences but are not strict requirements. Consider whether the story demonstrates moral seriousness, cultural insight, or compassionate understanding without being didactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility & Procedural/Format Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry and procedural constraints: open to British nationals/UK residents (18+); stories up to 8,000 words; blind submissions; five-judge panel; shortlist of five; winner announced at BBC Radio 4 broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with eligibility (nationality/residency, age) and length limits. Note the blind submission process (mitigates bias) and competitive structure; procedural features do not alter literary criteria but are required for valid entry. Prize information (£15,000) and panel rotation are administrative details.
